# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 2 (Bu-Vb Ss2)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Ss2
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya

**Title (English, from literature):** Physical contact with a woman

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kāyasaṁsagga-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 2) is the second rule in the Saṅghādisesa chapter of the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* within the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a monk overcome by lust who engages in physical contact with a woman incurs an offense entailing initial and subsequent meetings of the Saṅgha, resulting in formal suspension [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its associated narrative framing has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this precept is shared across all major early Buddhist monastic traditions, appearing in the Theravāda Pātimokkha and Parivāra, as well as the Prātimokṣa sūtras and Vinayavibhaṅgas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. Computational textual analysis via DharmaNexus confirms close Pali-internal reuse with adjacent Vinaya rules—most notably Saṅghādisesa 3, Saṅghādisesa 1, Saṅghādisesa 4, and Pārājika 2—and with canonical commentaries such as the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā* and subcommentaries including the *Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of this text with Tibetan Vinaya works—such as the *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003), *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105), and *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* (D0007A)—and Sanskrit Vinaya treatises [DharmaNexus]. None of the sampled secondary literature passages specifically discuss this rule, citing instead unrelated works containing typographical matches for section symbols [1–22].
